**8.7 Administration and Office**

The Administration and Office allocation of £4,800 covers the costs of printing, postage, the club's website hosting, and the annual audit fee. The audit fee has been confirmed at £1,500, which represents a small increase on the previous year. **8.2 Grounds and Maintenance**

The allocation of £18,500 for Grounds and Maintenance includes the scheduled replacement of the outfield mower, which the Groundsman has advised is now beyond economic repair. A quote of £6,750 has been received from Countrywide Groundcare for a replacement machine, and this will be purchased in early April subject to the usual three quotations rule. The remaining balance covers the annual contract for pitch renovation, line marking materials, and the hire of aeration equipment. The Facilities Officer has also requested that a contingency of £500 within this heading be reserved for weed treatment on the training pitches, which have shown signs of leatherjacket damage following the mild winter.

**8.3 Catering and Bar**

The Committee approved an allocation of £7,400 for Catering and Bar for 2025/26, which is included within the Match-day Operations heading shown in the summary table above. This is a new line item for the coming year, reflecting the decision to bring the bar and catering operation in-house rather than continue with the external contractor. The allocation covers the initial purchase of stock, minor equipment (a new coffee machine and a second fridge), and the wages of two part-time bar staff. The Catering Manager has prepared a separate trading budget, which projects a modest surplus of £1,200 for the year. A copy of this trading budget is attached at Annex A.

**8.4 Equipment and Kit**

The Equipment and Kit allocation of £12,400 includes £4,000 for the replacement of the senior men's match-day kit, which will be ordered from the club's usual supplier in June. The remaining £8,400 covers training balls, bibs, cones, first-aid supplies, and the repair of the goal nets and corner flags. The Kit Manager has noted that the current stock of size 5 match balls is low and has requested that 24 new balls be ordered for the start of pre-season. This request has been approved within the allocation.

**8.5 Coaching and Development**

The Coaching and Development allocation of £15,750 includes the cost of the FA-qualified coaches' fees for the senior and junior sections, as well as the club's contribution to coach education courses. Two volunteers are due to complete their FA Level 1 course in May, and their course fees (totalling £360) will be met from this budget. The allocation also includes £2,000 for the hire of indoor facilities during the winter months for the junior development centre.

**8.6 Junior Programme**

The Junior Programme allocation of £8,300 covers the costs of the mini-soccer and youth teams, including league entry fees, referees' fees for home matches, and the end-of-season presentation event. The Youth Development Officer has confirmed that the number of junior teams will remain at 12 for the coming season. A contribution of £1,000 from this heading has been earmarked for a summer football camp, which will be open to children in the local community.

**8.7 Administration and Office**

The Administration and Office allocation of £4,800 covers the costs of printing, postage, the club's website hosting, and the annual audit fee. The audit fee has been confirmed at £1,500, which represents a small increase on the previous year. The allocation also includes £500 for the renewal of the club's data protection registration with the Information Commissioner's Office and for the purchase of a new printer for the Finance Office.
